claims.feature: Graph view with editing on the graph
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: Graph view draws objects and arrays as linked nodes; a value is edited on the graph
unit:jsonx:graph: one node per object/array, primitives as fields, edges labelled, laid out left to right
unit:jsonx:graph: big documents are capped with a count of what was left out
ui:json-validator:2.2: Table view of an array of objects, editable, written back into the document
unit:jsonx:findTables: arrays of objects anywhere, largest first

claims.feature: Data-level compare, with hand-off to the Diff Checker's structure mode
claims.competitor: JSON Crack Premium / JSON Editor Online
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: Compare two documents by path; the Diff Checker's structure mode opens with both
unit:jsonx:compare: added, removed and changed paths; numbers compared exactly

claims.feature: JMESPath, JSON Query and jq transforms
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: Transform with JMESPath, JSON Query and jq, then use the result

claims.feature: Explicit JSON5, JSONC and JSON Lines modes
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: input modes: JSON5, JSONC and JSON Lines read explicitly; YAML, TOML and XML convert in
unit:jsonx:JSON5: comments, unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas, hex, signs, .5, line continuation
unit:jsonx:JSONC: comments and trailing commas only; JSON5 features are refused

claims.feature: 50 MB+ files in a Worker with a virtualised tree
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: a 60 MB file is read in a Worker; text and tree are virtual
ui:json-validator:2.2: input modes: JSON5, JSONC and JSON Lines read explicitly; YAML, TOML and XML convert in
ui:json-validator:2.2: XML and TOML out
unit:jsonx:XML -> JSON: attributes, repeated elements, text, CDATA, entities, namespaces
unit:jsonx:JSON -> XML: attributes, arrays repeat, names made valid, text escaped; round trip

claims.feature: Sample JSON generated from a schema
tests: ui:json-validator:2.2: sample JSON generated from a schema validates; the visual schema editor writes the schema
unit:jsonx:sample from schema: types, required, enum, const, default, formats, ranges, $ref, allOf, oneOf
ui:json-validator:2.2: sample JSON generated from a schema validates; the visual schema editor writes the schema
ui:json-validator:2.2 / A3: tree, JSONPath, types and conversions keep long numbers exactly
unit:json:A3: every view works on lossless numbers: JSONPath, filters, schema, inference, types, stats, CSV, SQL
